nodes.notes: Re-reads the ticket immediately before any write. Do not trust status passed in from the caller - stale caller data is the exact failure mode this guards against.

nodes.name: Ticket not solved or closed?
nodes.notes: Base status only - new/open/pending/hold pass, solved/closed are blocked. Deliberately enumerates the states we refuse to write to, so a new custom status cannot silently start blocking replies.

nodes.name: Skip: ticket already solved or closed
nodes.notes: Terminal. Reached when a duplicate or replayed webhook targets a ticket the automation has already finished. No Zendesk write on purpose - reopening it would re-queue it for agents and could re-fire the 2nd-message trigger.

parameters.content:
## Status guard

Blocks writes when the ticket is already `solved` or `closed`.

Why: Zendesk can deliver the same `ticket created` webhook a second time hours later (seen 2026-07-23, ~8h37m late). The automation then re-ran on the original first email and contradicted its own earlier reply.

Why base `status` and not a custom status id: the ticket API always returns `status` as a plain string, so this needs no `cs_project_config` column and behaves identically for every brand. `closed` is covered for free.

A legitimate customer follow-up is safe here - Zendesk auto-reopens a solved ticket on requester reply, so status is `open` by the time the 2nd-message flow runs.
